next_mission_recommendation.mission_title: Email Investigation Service - Smart Prioritization and Rate Limiting
next_mission_recommendation.mission_description: Implement intelligent investigation prioritization and rate limiting for the Email Investigation Service. Currently all investigations run with equal priority and there is no throttling mechanism. The mission should: (1) Add a priority scoring system to classify_email() that assigns priority 1-5 based on sender reputation, subject keywords, and time-sensitivity indicators. (2) Implement rate limiting in the daemon to cap concurrent investigations (e.g., max 3 simultaneous) with a priority queue that processes high-priority investigations first. (3) Add sender reputation tracking that learns from investigation outcomes - senders whose investigations frequently succeed get higher priority, repeat spam senders get deprioritized. (4) Add a GET /api/email/queue/priority endpoint showing the current priority queue state. (5) Add configurable rate limits to config.yaml (max_concurrent, cooldown_seconds). All changes should integrate with the existing daemon loop and queue_manager.py infrastructure.
next_mission_recommendation.rationale: The service currently processes 431+ investigations with a 99.3% success rate, but has no mechanism to handle load spikes or prioritize urgent investigations. With the hardening work complete (self-send filter, validation, digest), the next logical step is operational intelligence - making the service smarter about what it processes and when. The existing queue_manager.py and daemon infrastructure provide natural extension points for this work.

final_report.summary: Across 2 cycles, the Email Investigation Service at /home/vader/Email_Investigations/ was hardened with 4 core features in Cycle 1 (self-send filter, duration tracking, query param validation, daily digest method) and 4 integration tasks in Cycle 2 (digest scheduling in daemon main loop with persistent state, self-send filter end-to-end verification, digest preview API endpoint, full regression testing). The service processes emails via IMAP, classifies them, and runs autonomous investigations. All changes were validated with 71 tests (13 self-tests, 39 adversarial, 19 live regression) achieving 100% pass rate. The live service remained healthy throughout with 431 completed investigations and a 99.3% success rate.
key_achievements: Self-send email filter prevents infinite investigation loops by classifying emails from the service's own address as PURGE before any subject-based routing
Investigation duration tracking via elapsed_seconds field on ProcessedEmail, set at completion in both thread-based and sync-based code paths
Analytics duration_distribution populates correctly with <5m/5-10m/10-20m/20-30m/>30m bucketing using elapsed_seconds with RFC 2822 timestamp fallback
Centralized query parameter validation (_parse_int_param) on inbox/processed/investigations endpoints blocks injection attacks, type confusion, and out-of-range values
Daily digest method sends HTML email summary with per-investigation details, success rate, and average duration
Digest scheduling wired into daemon main loop with _last_digest_date persisted to state file, surviving restarts and preventing duplicate sends
GET /api/email/digest/preview endpoint returns JSON digest stats for dashboard integration
HTML escaping in digest email subjects prevents XSS injection
71/71 tests passing across self-test, adversarial, and live regression categories
challenges_overcome: RFC 2822 vs ISO date format mismatch - received_at timestamps used RFC 2822 format while analytics code expected ISO; added email.utils.parsedate_to_datetime() fallback
Duration tracking write-back gap - elapsed_seconds was computed but not always persisted back to state; fixed in both _run_investigation_thread() and _handle_investigation_completion()
Digest retry storms - without error-path state persistence, a failed digest send would retry every poll cycle; fixed by persisting _last_digest_date even on failure
Edge cases in duration analytics - NaN, Infinity, negative values, and corrupted timestamps all required careful handling to prevent analytics corruption
Self-send filter positioning - filter must execute before subject-based routing to prevent emails with 'investigation' in subject from bypassing the self-send check
lessons_learned: Position security filters (like self-send) at the TOP of classification logic, before any content-based routing that could match and bypass them
Always persist scheduling state to survive process restarts - in-memory-only tracking is fragile for daemon processes
Adversarial testing catches real bugs: Unicode lookalikes, null bytes, scientific notation, and type confusion are all real attack vectors on query parameters
Duration tracking requires write-back at EVERY completion code path, not just the primary one - async/thread/sync paths all need coverage
Functional testing against the live service (19 endpoint tests) catches integration issues that unit tests miss entirely
